title: Placenta praevia
sub: Eleven stops: what praevia is, why it happens, how it changes week by week, why it bleeds, how to diagnose it safely, and how to manage it from the first bleed through the drugs, delivery and haemorrhage. Every stop zooms in, and a lens shows that part from a new angle. Drag the timeline under the pelvis to move through the pregnancy.
foot: Sources: RCOG Green-top Guidelines 27a (placenta praevia and placenta accreta, 2018), 63 (antepartum haemorrhage) and 52 (postpartum haemorrhage), NICE NG25 (preterm labour and birth), and Silver et al. 2006 for accreta risk by number of caesareans. Doses are teaching values, so check them against your local protocol and the BNF before using them clinically. Drawings are schematic. Controls: ← → move between stops, Space plays or pauses, and Shift + ← → moves through the weeks.

stage.aria: Sagittal section of a pregnant pelvis: abdominal wall, bladder, uterus with placenta and fetus, cervix, vagina, rectum and sacrum. The uterus grows with the weeks shown on the timeline.

strip.aria: Pregnancy timeline in weeks. Drag, or use Shift and the arrow keys, to move through the pregnancy.
